Use Case Description (2000 Characters):
The Job Monitoring Agent gives operations, support and business teams one place to see which scheduled jobs have failed in SAP Cloud ALM, why they failed and who needs to act, without logging into a monitoring tool.
Scheduled jobs such as data loads, interface runs and month-end processing keep business processes running. When a job fails, downstream processes stop, often unnoticed until users complain. The agent automatically pulls job run data and logs from SAP Cloud ALM Job and Automation Monitoring every minute and stores the history on SAP Business Technology Platform. A web dashboard shows key figures, the list of failed jobs and the full detail and log messages of every run.
For each failed job, users can start an AI analysis. An SAP AI agent, grounded in SAP Help documentation, explains the most likely causes (at most two) and the documented resolution steps in plain language. The AI is only used to explain failures; all figures come directly from the stored data, so every user sees the same numbers.
The agent also warns the responsible job scheduler: one grouped e-mail per scheduler lists the failed runs, and the same failure is never mailed twice.
Other agents, for example SAP Joule, can query the job data through the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol with a dedicated read-only client. Access for people is controlled centrally through role collections (Viewer and Admin) in SAP BTP. The agent only reads data and never changes, restarts or cancels jobs in the source system.
Challenges & Business Drivers (500 Chara: Scheduled application jobs run period-end closes, data loads and interface runs overnight, and one failure can stall every process that follows. Failures sit in monitoring lists until someone checks, the logs are technical, and finding the SAP-documented fix takes time. Job owners are not told directly, so alerts are missed or repeated, deadlines slip and support tickets pile up. Teams need one failure view, grounded fix guidance and a single warning per owner.
Solutions (500 Characters): The agent pulls job runs and logs from SAP Cloud ALM on a schedule, keeps the history in SAP HANA Cloud and shows failures in a dashboard. An SAP AI agent explains likely causes and documented fixes per failed job. Grouped e-mail warnings reach the responsible job schedulers. An A2A interface lets other agents read the same data. Access is managed through BTP role collections.
Benefits (500 Characters): Faster detection and resolution of failed jobs and fewer blocked business processes. Guided root-cause help reduces dependence on expert knowledge. Proactive e-mails reach job owners without manual monitoring. One consistent data source for dashboard, e-mails and agents. Read-only design avoids any risk to the source system. Central, auditable access control.
Services & Applications (500 Characters): SAP Business Technology Platform (Cloud Foundry runtime); SAP Cloud Application Programming Model (Node.js); SAP HANA Cloud; SAP Cloud ALM (Job and Automation Monitoring, Analytics and Logs APIs); SAP AI Core / Generative AI Hub; SAP Job Scheduling Service; SAP Authorization and Trust Management Service (XSUAA); SAP BTP Destination Service; Application Router; Microsoft Graph (Mail); Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol.
Prerequisites (500 Characters): SAP Cloud ALM with Job and Automation Monitoring set up for the connected systems, and API access via an OAuth client. An SAP BTP subaccount with Cloud Foundry, SAP HANA Cloud, Job Scheduling, Destination and XSUAA. SAP AI Core with a grounded model. A Microsoft Graph app with Mail.Send for warnings. Users assigned to the JobFailureMonitor role collections.
